title: Volta Redonda: the Companhia Siderúrgica Nacional, 1941
summary: Brazil’s first integrated steelworks was created as a state company on 9 April 1941, by decree of Getúlio Vargas under the Estado Novo, after an agreement between the Brazilian and American governments — the Washington Accords — for a plant that would supply the Allies with steel during the war and help Brazil develop after it. The money came from the Export-Import Bank of the United States, because American private capital would not put it up. The site chosen was the Paraíba valley, which the commission’s president Colonel Macedo Soares argued for and which had fallen into decadence with the decline of coffee in Rio de Janeiro state. The Presidente Vargas Steelworks at Volta Redonda began production in 1946. On Wikipedia’s account of Vargas, the bargain was explicit: in exchange for raw materials the United States provided equipment, technical assistance and the financing of the mill, settled in July 1940.
